  "question": "What has been proposed to reduce the risk of image classifiers giving unreliable answers on unfamiliar or maliciously altered images, and by what mechanism?",
  "reference_answer": "The proposed intervention is to train convolutional neural networks on human-derived soft labels, such as the distributions of human categorization judgments in CIFAR-10H, rather than only single-category hard labels. Hard labels assign each image to one category without expressing uncertainty. Human soft labels instead retain uncertainty and graded category membership. Learning to predict these judgments encourages networks to learn more perceptually relevant category distributions, making them more tolerant of noise and allowing performance to deteriorate more gradually. This improves generalization to images unlike the training examples and resilience to adversarial manipulation. The reported benefits exceed those obtained by adding random label noise, suggesting that the structure of human judgments—not merely a noise-based regularization effect—is useful.",
